standard-dialogue-without-book-o-piracy.npc: Arr? Be ye wantin' te go on account with our gang o' fillibusters?
The powder monkey be takin' a caulk after gettin' rowdy on bumboo, so there be plenty of room for ye.

standard-dialogue-without-book-o-piracy.player: I'll just be over here if you need me.

standard-dialogue-with-book-o-piracy.npc: I got fish, you got gold?

options.text: Yes, but I don't want your fish.

steps.player: Yes, but I don't want your fish.

steps.npc: Then what are ye doin' in a fish shop? Looking fer work?

steps.player: Possibly, do you have any quests?

steps.npc: I dunno, I haven't gone through the last catch yet. What sort of a fish is it?

steps.player: A quest isn't a type of fish!

steps.npc: Then I don't have any, and yer wastin' my time!
Ye wanna know what happened to my legs?
Yer too much of a lilly-livered, hat wearin' landlubber to know what happened to my legs!

steps.player: No I'm not! I've seen some freaky stuff! I can take it!

steps.npc: All right, [lad/lass], since yer so insistent, I'll tell ye.
See, I was clingin' onto a barrel, me ship havin' just had an encounter with this albatross.
The sea was thrashin' and wild, but not so wild that I didn't see the fins of some sharks closin' in on me.
I managed to yank a sliver of wood from the barrel just as one of them grabbed me from below, but I slipped down the things throat by about two feet before I managed te kill it.
A passin' ship saw the sharks and knew there would be survivors in the water. They sent a longboat and picked me up, but not before the sharks had taken off my legs.
And that [lad/lass] is why they call me two feet Charley, because they found me jammed two feet down a shark's throat.

steps.player: I think I'm gonna be sick...

steps.npc: I knew ye couldn't handle the truth!
